pr_body:
the hostport manager was not taking into consideration the hostIP
when binding the socket of the hostPort, causing that the same
HostPort can not be used with different IP addresses.

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug
/kind failing-test

```release-note
kubelet: fixes a bug in the HostPort dockershim implementation that caused the conformance test "HostPort validates that there is no conflict between pods with same hostPort but different hostIP and protocol" to fail.
```

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98648

/assign
So, this job is different that the one that we have in presubmit?
ping @BenTheElder

I see , this is in informing, the problem is that HostPort implementation in dockershim has a known bug, but since we started the deprecation is not worth the effort to fix it https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94382
the failing test is a conformance test ... are we saying that deployments using dockershim cannot be conformant in 1.20+?

> So, this job is different that the one that we have in presubmit?

I mean, the spec for a presubmit and any other type of job is not identical, so yes. But this job should more or less be the same IIRC.
do any of our presubmits running this test use dockershim? cc @dims

I don't think we are running blocking presubmits with dockershim currently, but we also can't run presubmits with all implementations of pluggable bits.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/94382#issuecomment-685188550 would seem to suggest we should actually fix dockershim though, i'm not sure where the implication otherwise is coming from.
To be clear, dockershim never passed this test, it only did because the test was wrong

Linking to a prior example of presubmit / periodic container runtime mismatch example (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96495). @liggitt @BenTheElder at the time we were working on the referenced bug we considered whether we should be consistent with various plugins we were testing against in presubmit vs periodic. However, in many cases such as this one, we are getting more coverage by testing against different ones. It would be nice to establish some policy around to what extent we test against various CRI / CNI / etc., similar to how we are formalizing our rigor around testing various platforms (https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-release/issues/1337).

> Linking to a prior example of presubmit / periodic container runtime mismatch example (#96495). @liggitt @BenTheElder at the time we were working on the referenced bug we considered whether we should be consistent with various plugins we were testing against in presubmit vs periodic. 

In this case I don't think there's any mismatch, dockershim is just not in cluster e2e presubtmit

> However, in many cases such as this one, we are getting more coverage by testing against different ones. It would be nice to establish some policy around to what extent we test against various CRI / CNI / etc., similar to how we are formalizing our rigor around testing various platforms (kubernetes/sig-release#1337).

We've intentionally not advertised these to avoid some kind of favored vendor status or vendors trying to cram every last option into presubmit. SIG node started the policy of not supporting / endorsing / advertising any of the runtimes IIRC.

KIND goes one step further and ships a stripped down networking implementation ourselves.
